title: Midnight at a glance
caption: Midnight at a glance. A protocol designer touches five layers: wallets and dapps, the indexer, the node and its ledger, the Cardano partner chain, and the network underneath. Contract events leave the ledger in public form; nothing in the stack carries a private event.
labels: Midnight node: ledger, Compact contracts, zero-knowledge proofs
Public event (emit): 32 B name + 256 B payload

title: Public versus private events
caption: What an observer learns from a public contract event and from a Confidential Message. The public event shows its name, payload, time and the contract that emitted it. The Confidential Message shows only a fixed-size MPE Envelope on a Shard at a time.
labels: Public event: name, payload, contract, block time, reacting transaction
Observer sees: who reacted, when, to what
Observer sees: size class, shard, time

title: Adversaries and what they observe
caption: The adversary classes and their vantage points along the path of one Message: a local observer such as one relay or the Indexer (R), colluding infrastructure (C), an active network adversary (A), a global passive observer (G), and a chain observer.

title: The design space
caption: Families of prior art placed by what they hide and what they cost. Flooding and mixing hide the most and cost the most; topic gossip is cheap and hides little; retrieval schemes move the cost to the receiver or the server.

title: Five architecture options
caption: The five architecture options for Midnight. Option 2, a GossipSub sidecar overlay anchored on the ledger, is recommended; Option 1, the ledger and Indexer alone, survives as the ledger lane.
labels: Option 2: Hybrid, GossipSub sidecar overlay with ledger anchoring
Option 4: Mix network or PIR delivery

title: From decisions to requirements
caption: From ten decision areas to twelve requirement areas, the 625-entry requirement set, and the 137-requirement prototype core.

title: Reference system architecture
caption: The reference system. Publishers seal a Message into an MPE Envelope and send it to a Bus Node; Bus Nodes relay it through sharded GossipSub meshes; Subscribers recognise their Messages locally; Store Nodes retain MPE Envelopes; an anchorer posts Anchors to the Bus Registry; the ledger lane uses the Indexer.
labels: Ledger lane: Misc events on the ledger

title: Envelope layout
caption: Envelope layout and size classes. An 8-byte fixed header and a 512-byte admission slot precede the sealed body. The four classes give wire lengths of 776, 1,544, 4,616 and 16,904 bytes.
labels: Sealed body: 256 B, 1,024 B, 4,096 B or 16,384 B

title: Life of a Message
caption: The life of one Message: seal, admit, gossip, recognise, anchor and react.

title: Experiment harness
caption: The planned experiment harness. A seeded schedule will drive GossipSub swarms; each scenario will produce a result file that a checker compares with fixed thresholds.

title: Envelope overhead by class
caption: Fixed overhead and payload capacity of the four size classes.

title: Roadmap
caption: The staged plan from proof of concept to production, with the evidence each stage needs.
labels: Stage 0: models, simulation and proof of concept
